children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose on Monday, led by chipmakers after a rally in US semiconductor stocks in the previous session and upbeat domestic export data.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was up 101.16 points, or 1.47%, at 6,995.39, as of 0134 GMT.
** Wall Street closed a volatile week on a muted note on Friday as benchmark US Treasury yields topped 5%, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
rose 2.8%.
** South Korea's exports for the first 20 days of this month hit a record high on a surge in chip sales, customs data showed.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 4.02% and peer SK Hynix
gained 0.92%, leading the benchmark index higher.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 2.75%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 1.10% and 1.64%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 0.77%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 0.14%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 310 shares advanced, while 549 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 113 billion won ($81.64 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,384.9 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.04% higher than its previous close at 1,385.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.05 point to 102.24.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 1.0 basis point to 4.037%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 0.5 basis point to 4.455%.
